finding.claim: Unauthenticated attacker can make the server fetch arbitrary URLs via /logo. The only host check is a substring match on 'example.io', which an attacker satisfies by placing it in the query string, e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?example.io. The response body is returned to the caller (full-read SSRF).
finding.sink: main.go:36 http.Get(raw) using default client; redirects followed with no re-validation; body copied to response at main.go:38

trace.note: strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") — substring check, not strict set membership; bypassed by example.io in query string
http.Get(raw) — SSRF sink; no scheme or host allowlist, redirects followed unchecked
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) — response returned to attacker

finding.guards_checked: main.go:32 strings.Contains substring check: bypassable, does not close per ssrf/SKILL.md. No scheme restriction. No hostname set membership. No CheckRedirect on http.Get default client. No IP-range blocking. Route unauthenticated. Triage Step 0 answered (unauthenticated external user; single GET; request triggers fetch; reads internal/metadata responses). Severity HIGH; Validation Tier 0.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is main.go:32 strings.Contains(raw, "example.io"), a substring match that the claimed payload satisfies via the query string. No scheme restriction, host allowlist, IP-range blocking, or redirect check exists on the path. The `trusted` map and `noRedirect` helper at main.go:10-12 are used only by the separate /cdn handler (main.go:20-24), not by /logo.
verdict.reason:
Source r.FormValue("logo") at main.go:31 is attacker-controlled on an unauthenticated route registered at main.go:43 and served on :8081 (main.go:44); the substring check at main.go:32 does not close it, and http.Get(raw) at main.go:36 uses the default client that follows redirects and io.Copy at main.go:38 returns the body to the caller.</reason>
</invoke>

finding.claim: Closed candidate, not a finding: /cdn handler is safe. Source main.go:15 r.FormValue("u"). Exact map membership on u.Hostname() (main.go:20, trusted map at main.go:10). Client uses CheckRedirect returning http.ErrUseLastResponse (main.go:24), so no redirect escape. Sink main.go:25 fetches the same string that was checked. Userinfo bypass fails because Hostname() strips it. Non-SSRF note: main.go:25 ignores error, nil resp deref at main.go:26 (panic recovered per request by net/http; OUT/availability domain).
finding.guards_checked: Exact hostname set membership (main.go:20); redirects disabled (main.go:12, main.go:24); userinfo confusion rejected by Hostname(); port not restricted but host is trusted, so out of scope.

verdict.guard_found: main.go:20 exact map membership on u.Hostname() against trusted = {"cdn.example.io"} (main.go:10); main.go:12 and main.go:24 CheckRedirect returns http.ErrUseLastResponse, so redirects are not followed. The fetched string at main.go:25 is the same u.String() that was checked. Userinfo is stripped by Hostname(), so the check matches the host Go's client connects to.
verdict.reason: The sink at main.go:25 fetches only when u.Hostname() exactly matches "cdn.example.io" (main.go:20), and redirects are disabled at main.go:24, so the attacker-controlled u at main.go:15 cannot reach an arbitrary host. The main.go:26 nil dereference when the request errors is a panic/availability issue, not SSRF.
